comparator.name: Biomedical Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: UvA builds from cells, genetics, anatomy and physiology to laboratory work, immunology, cell imaging and genome analysis. This plan illustrates Frontiers in Medical Biology. Students then take electives and complete an independent biomedical research placement.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: Frontiers in Medical Biology extends the common molecular, genomic and experimental research sequence across biomedical systems. Neurobiology centres on the nervous system and Patient Oriented Research on research closer to clinical applications. This choice follows the breadth of the UvA core independently of UCR fit. The standard 18 EC project leaves 12 EC open.

notes.text: UvA combines an integrated laboratory sequence, dedicated omics study and a required research placement. The UCR options combine individual courses in biomedical science, population health or quantitative methods. Their laboratory and research experiences differ from UvA’s required sequence.

audience.programmeDescription: UvA Biomedical Sciences studies how the human body works and how disease develops. The programme combines laboratory work, data analysis and independent biomedical research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options explore disease mechanisms, population health or quantitative methods. UvA brings these areas together in a specialist biomedical curriculum.
